findings_detail.description: With `initialize == true`, the startup path now takes its reference time from `m_gameTime` (lines 1781 and 1792) instead of `time(NULL)`. The sibling `InitCurrencyResetTime` at line 1803 deliberately uses `time(NULL)` with the comment "game time not yet init", and `InitDailyQuestResetTime` also still uses `time(NULL)`. I cannot see where `m_gameTime` is set relative to this call. If it is 0 or stale here, `NextMonthlyQuestReset(m_gameTime, stored, true)` returns a date in the past (Feb 1970 for 0), which is written to `saved_variables` and makes the first `Update` fire a monthly quest reset on every restart.
findings_detail.fix_sketch: Use `time(NULL)` as `now` when `initialize` is true (keep `m_gameTime` for the runtime re-arm), or assert/guarantee `m_gameTime` is set before this call.

findings_detail.description: The newly exported `NextMonthlyQuestReset` is documented in World.h as returning "local midnight on the first of the following month", but `localTm` keeps the `tm_isdst` of `now` when passed to `mktime`. This is carried over from the old code. If a DST change falls between `now` and the 1st, the result is typically shifted by an hour (23:00 on the last day or 01:00 on the 1st). In the 23:00 case the reset fires, recomputes within the same month, and fires again at 00:00, which is the double reset this PR aims to remove. The new tests only assert midnight on rows that do not cross a DST change.
findings_detail.fix_sketch: Set `localTm.tm_isdst = -1;` before `mktime(&localTm)` so the target date's own DST state is used.

findings_detail.description: The Staging1 branch arms the cipher, sends SMSG_RESUME_COMMS and promotes on ANY first framed packet, not only CMSG_AUTH_CONTINUED_SESSION. Because arming moved from the banner to this packet, that packet is now read fully in clear, and any other opcode falls through to m_gateway.Deliver(m_session, ...) under the session bound by the address-matched ticket. A peer sharing the client's address (NAT, same host) that reaches the stream-1 port first can inject one arbitrary plaintext opcode into the victim's session and take over its stream 1.
findings_detail.fix_sketch: At the top of the Staging1 branch, log and return false if opcode != CMSG_AUTH_CONTINUED_SESSION, before arming, sending resume or promoting.

findings_detail.description: CMSG_AUTH_CONTINUED_SESSION is accepted with no validation: not the 36-byte length, not the echoed connect-to key, not the SHA-1(account || session key || server seed) digest. Before this PR the first stream-1 header had to decrypt under the session key, which was a weak implicit proof of key possession. Now the only thing binding the socket to the session is its source address, and whoever wins the race then receives the session's stream-1 traffic, whose payloads are not encrypted.
findings_detail.fix_sketch: Carry the account name and connect-to key on RedirectTicket, recompute the digest with m_redirectKey and m_seed, and reject on mismatch or wrong payload size before arming and promoting.

findings_detail.description: SendResumeComms() runs before PromoteToSlotOne() can fail (session gone, or a superseded redirect generation). On failure the client has already been told to move this socket into stream 1; per the comment at lines 246-248 it then retires whatever held that slot and flushes its queue onto a socket the server closes on the next line. A stale redirect answer can therefore displace the client's newer live stream 1 and lose the client's queued stream-1 packets.
findings_detail.fix_sketch: Check that m_links is alive and the generation is still expected before sending SMSG_RESUME_COMMS, or have AttachSlotOne send it under its lock just before flushing the held queue.

findings_detail.description: The generator claims a reproducible table from a fixed mt19937_64 seed, but several EmitCase calls consume the RNG in more than one argument, e.g. `EmitCase(RandomBits(256 + int(rng() % 3) * 32), RandomBits(64), BigNumber(d))` (also lines 210, 215, 238, 243, 253, 268). C++ leaves argument evaluation order unspecified, and MSVC, GCC and Clang differ in practice. Regenerating CryptoGoldenVectors.h on another compiler therefore yields different operands, so the checked-in table cannot be reproduced or audited from the seed.
findings_detail.fix_sketch: Draw each random operand into a named local in a fixed statement order before calling EmitCase, e.g. `BigNumber a = RandomBits(...); BigNumber b = RandomBits(64); EmitCase(a, b, n);`.
